claims.text: This is an active wheat bakery. All products are made with wheat, whole wheat, and rye flours. Flour dust and cross-contamination are inherent to the environment. Not suitable for celiac disease or serious gluten intolerance.
The kitchen handles dairy and egg ingredients (standard croissants alongside vegan croissants). Cross-contact risk for strict vegans cannot be ruled out without direct confirmation from the baker.

No allergy-handling protocols are documented in any source. The shop is a very small one-person operation; contact via phone (026-405-4769), Instagram, or LINE before visiting if allergies are a concern.
Core breads contain no added sugar, oil, or additives. Vegan croissants (no butter, milk, or eggs) are a confirmed menu item.
All ingredients are domestic; no artificial additives or preservatives used.

name: ポルカドットカフェ (Polka Dot Cafe)

claims.text: No cross-contamination controls have been documented. The kitchen produces tempura (wheat batter) and other wheat-containing dishes alongside everything else, with no published separation procedures.
Standard soy sauce is used throughout the washoku set meals, marinades (e.g., ginger pork shogayaki), and dipping preparations. No tamari or gluten-free soy sauce has been mentioned in any source.

Dashi-simmered vegetable dishes and miso soup are core to every set meal; bonito dashi (katsuo) is standard in washoku cooking and is not flagged as absent. Egg dishes (tamagoyaki, shirasu omelette) are regularly listed among the rotating side dishes.

One reviewer noted that staff accommodated a request to reduce rice and miso soup portions and offered refills on request, suggesting general flexibility, but no allergy-specific protocol has been documented.
The pumpkin karaage side dish uses potato starch and rice flour as its coating — incidentally gluten-free frying, though not offered as a dedicated GF item.
The set meal format naturally includes many vegetable-based small dishes, giving partial accommodation more room than a single-dish restaurant would.

name: リストランテ カンパネッラ (Ristorante Campanella)

claims.text: Pasta is a menu centrepiece; wheat flour is in active use throughout the kitchen. No information about cross-contamination controls was found on any source.
The menu features Japanese-inflected Italian-French dishes. Standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat; use in sauces or marinades cannot be ruled out without direct inquiry.
Butter, cream, cheese, and other dairy are standard in Italian-French cuisine; shared preparation surfaces and cookware are expected. No vegan-separated prep protocols are mentioned anywhere.

No allergen menu, staff allergy training, or dietary accommodation protocol is mentioned on any reviewed source. Advance phone contact (026-233-4560) or email (campanella.if@nifty.com) is the only available channel for dietary queries.
The kitchen grows most vegetables at the chef's own farm in Takayama Village, meaning produce quality and provenance are unusually transparent for an Italian restaurant in this region.
All dishes from antipasto through dessert are entirely house-made, giving the kitchen full control over ingredients — a meaningful advantage for custom dietary requests made well in advance.

No allergen or cross-contamination information is published by the restaurant. The kitchen is small and shared; wheat is present throughout (conventional soy sauce, miso, pickles, waffle batter). Cross-contamination risk must be assumed high.
The menu uses conventional Japanese miso and implied soy sauce (miso-dressed dishes, pickles, stir-fries). Neither tamari nor gluten-free soy sauce is mentioned anywhere.
All lunch sets contain animal protein (chicken, mackerel). Miso soup is made with house-made miso and almost certainly fish-based dashi. There is no plant-based preparation pathway.

name: 信州門前ベーカリー 蔵 (Shinshu Monzen Bakery Kura)

claims.text: Standard wheat bakery environment — wheat flour is the primary ingredient throughout the entire production process. Cross-contamination with wheat is essentially certain. Not suitable for anyone with celiac disease or serious gluten sensitivity.

No allergen menu is published. Hot sandwich fillings (venison curry, croque monsieur, sausage baguette) likely contain wheat-based soy sauce and other gluten-bearing condiments, but specifics are not disclosed.
Butter, eggs, dairy, and meat are core ingredients used throughout the bakery's product range. There is no plant-based section or allergen separation protocol mentioned in any source.
No allergen handling procedures or staff allergy training information has been published by the bakery. Contact the shop directly at 050-8883-6606 for specific dietary enquiries.

name: 信州 おいも工房 (Shinshu Oimo Kobo)

claims.text: No allergen chart or cross-contamination information is available online. The shop uses shared preparation equipment; dedicated fryer status is unknown. Celiacs cannot assume safety without asking staff directly.
No soy sauce-based items identified on the menu. Shinshu miso seasoning used on some kenpi flavors may contain barley (麦麹), which is not GF. Confirm before ordering miso-flavored items.
Gelato and shakes are made with Shinshu dairy milk and are prepared at the same counter as plant-based items. No information on dedicated utensils for vegan preparation.
No information found about English-language allergy communication or dedicated allergy protocols. The shop is a small walk-up stall; allergy inquiries in Japanese are advisable before ordering.

Core menu items — roasted sweet potato (熟成焼き芋) and plain honey daigaku-imo — are single-ingredient preparations with no obvious gluten sources, making them among the safer choices for those avoiding wheat.
Sweet potatoes are naturally gluten-free and the shop's entire concept is built around them, meaning the majority of menu items start from a GF-compatible base ingredient.

name: 信州善光寺 薬王院 (Shinshu Zenkoji Yakuoin)

claims.text: No information on dedicated fryers or cross-contamination protocols is publicly available. Tempura is a core menu item, so a shared fryer with wheat-battered items must be assumed unless confirmed otherwise.
Standard Japanese soy sauce (contains wheat) is the default in shojin ryori kitchens. No tamari or GF soy sauce alternatives are mentioned anywhere in public sources.
Shojin ryori is inherently plant-based; cross-contact with animal products is structurally unlikely in this kitchen, though no formal certification exists.
The temple's tourism board listing states allergy accommodations are available ('アレルギー食対応可') and dietary/religious needs can be discussed on inquiry. Contact at least two days in advance.

Dashi is made exclusively from kombu and shiitake soaking liquid — no bonito, no fish stock, no meat-based broth anywhere in the kitchen. This is structurally safer for fish-allergic guests than most Japanese restaurants.
The menu is entirely plant-based by religious tradition, eliminating the main animal-product cross-contact risks common in omnivore kitchens.

name: SOBA＆DINER 戸隠つきや 門前 (Soba & Diner Togakure Tsukiya Monzen)

claims.text: Tempura is a menu staple here (かき揚げ丼, 天丼, 天ぷら盛). Fryer oil is almost certainly shared; no dedicated GF fryer is documented.
Tsuyu (dipping broth) and likely all cooking sauces use standard Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat. No wheat-free soy sauce alternative is mentioned on any source.
Fish-based dashi (katsuobushi) is used in the tsuyu and broth. Duck (鴨ねぎ) and horse meat (ユッケ) appear on the menu. No plant-based dashi alternative documented.

No allergy menu, allergy questionnaire, or documented staff allergy protocol found across any source. Phone reservations are accepted (026-233-8028); celiac or vegan diners should call ahead in Japanese to discuss needs.

Buckwheat (soba) is naturally gluten-free in its pure form. If the shop uses 十割そば (100% buckwheat, no wheat binder), the noodles themselves could be GF — but this has not been confirmed for this restaurant.
